sentence:
We will prove that the three lines
  H_AO_A, H_BO_B, H_CO_C
are concurrent.
sentence-category-reason: Restates the goal of the problem without providing strategy or reasoning.

sentence: (Any proof showing that these three lines meet at one point is acceptable.
sentence-category-reason: Meta-comment about acceptability; transitional note without problem-solving content.

sentence: ) One nice solution is to prove that, in fact, each line H_XO_X is perpendicular to the side opposite X (that is, H_AO_A ⊥ BC, etc.) so that they become the three “altitudes” of a certain pedal triangle.
sentence-category-reason: Proposes a strategy: prove perpendicularities to get concurrency.

sentence: (In our situation the pedal triangle is that of the feet of the altitudes of ABC.
sentence-category-reason: Explains what specific pedal triangle is considered; conceptual clarification.

sentence: ) Since the three altitudes of any triangle meet at its orthocenter the result follows.
sentence-category-reason: Draws a logical conclusion using a known theorem to link plan to result.

sentence: (Several other approaches are possible.
sentence-category-reason: Meta-comment noting multiple approaches; no mathematical content.

sentence: Below is one acceptable solution.
sentence-category-reason: Transitional statement introducing a solution; meta-level.
Section header; organizational marker without mathematical content.

sentence: Assume we have a triangle ABC with circumcenter O.
sentence-category-reason: Restates the given setup from the problem.

sentence:
For each vertex (say A) define:
 • Let H_A be the foot of the perpendicular from A onto the opposite side BC.
sentence-category-reason: Introduces/defines a constructed point; setting notation.

sentence: • Extend line AO (note that O is the circumcenter of ABC) and let A′ be its second intersection with the circle through B, O, and C.
sentence-category-reason: Defines A′ via a construction; setting up objects used later.

sentence: • From A′ drop perpendiculars to the two sides through A: let D be the foot on AB and E be the foot on AC.
sentence-category-reason: Defines D and E via perpendicular drops; construction step.

sentence: • Finally, define O_A to be the circumcenter of triangle D H_A E.
sentence-category-reason: Defines O_A as a circumcenter of a triangle; construction/notation.

sentence: In the same way we define points H_B, O_B and H_C, O_C.
sentence-category-reason: Extends the same constructions to other vertices; setting notation.
Section header; organizational marker.

sentence: (1) Show that DE ∥ BC.
sentence-category-reason: States a subgoal to be proved as part of the solution strategy.

sentence:
A good first observation is that, by the construction of D and E, we have
  A′D ⊥ AB  and  A′E ⊥ AC.
sentence-category-reason: Infers perpendicular relations from the construction; conceptual setup.

sentence:
One may show by chasing angles (and using the fact that A′ instead of A lies on the circle through B, O, C) that
  ∠(DE, AB) = ∠(BC, AB).
sentence-category-reason: Explains angle-chasing reasoning leading to an angle equality.

sentence: In other words, DE is parallel to BC.
sentence-category-reason: Concludes parallelism from the established angle equality.

sentence: (A similar proof shows that in the analogous constructions at B and C one obtains lines parallel to CA and AB respectively.
sentence-category-reason: Extends the reasoning to analogous cases at B and C.

sentence: (2) Then show that H_AO_A ⊥ DE.
sentence-category-reason: Announces the next step to prove a perpendicularity relation.

sentence: Since O_A is the circumcenter of triangle D H_A E (that is, the center of the circle through D, H_A and E) the line H_AO_A is perpendicular to the chord DE (a standard fact in circle geometry).
sentence-category-reason: Uses a known circle property to deduce a perpendicular; explanatory deduction without calculation.

sentence:
But since DE ∥ BC by (1), we deduce that
  H_AO_A ⊥ BC.
sentence-category-reason: Infers a new perpendicular from a parallelism previously established.

sentence:
The same argument shows that
  H_BO_B ⊥ CA  and  H_CO_C ⊥ AB.
sentence-category-reason: Extends the same reasoning cyclically to other vertices.
Section heading indicating a transition to concluding remarks.

sentence: Now, consider the three lines L_A = H_AO_A, L_B = H_BO_B, and L_C = H_CO_C.
sentence-category-reason: Introduces notation for the three lines to be discussed.

sentence:
We have proved that
  L_A ⊥ BC,  L_B ⊥ CA,  L_C ⊥ AB.
sentence-category-reason: Confirms the previously established perpendicular relationships.

sentence: That is, the line from the foot of the altitude H_A is perpendicular to BC and similarly for the others.
sentence-category-reason: Rephrases and interprets the established perpendicularities.

sentence: It is a well–known fact that the three altitudes of any triangle are concurrent (they meet at the orthocenter).
sentence-category-reason: Recalls a known theorem about concurrency of altitudes.

sentence: (In our case, the “triangle” whose altitudes we are considering is the “foot–triangle” having vertices H_A, H_B, H_C.
sentence-category-reason: Identifies the specific triangle to which the theorem is applied.

sentence: ) Therefore, the three lines H_AO_A, H_BO_B, H_CO_C are concurrent.
sentence-category-reason: States the main conclusion of concurrency.
Section heading marking a transition to closing comments.

sentence: Any solution that shows, in one way or another, that H_AO_A ⊥ BC (and cyclically for the other vertices) and then appeals to the well–known concurrence of the three altitudes of a triangle is acceptable.
sentence-category-reason: Describes a general acceptable solution approach.

sentence: (There are also analytic and inversion proofs.
sentence-category-reason: Mentions alternative possible approaches.

sentence: Thus we have shown that the three lines H_AO_A, H_BO_B, H_CO_C meet at a common point, completing the proof.
sentence-category-reason: Restates the final result, completing the proof.
